quality_guards: DSEAR risk depends on the substance, quantity, process, containment, ventilation, ignition sources, workforce and emergency arrangements.
HSE DSEAR guidance is workplace-, substance-, process-, control- and time-specific and is not an exact parcel-level fire or explosion probability.
COSHH risk depends on the substance, concentration, route, duration, process, workforce, controls and maintenance condition.
COSHH assessment evidence is substance-, task-, worker-, exposure-, control- and time-specific and is not an exact parcel-level disease probability.
Emergency effectiveness depends on the hazard, scenario, equipment, staffing, training, communications, access and response time.
COSHH emergency guidance is incident-, workplace-, substance-, responder-, equipment- and time-specific and is not an exact parcel-level emergency outcome.
Biological-agent risk depends on the agent, hazard group, activity, route, dose, containment, worker susceptibility and available treatment.
The Approved List is agent-, laboratory-, task-, control- and time-specific and is not an exact parcel-level infection probability.
Deliberate biological work risk depends on agent classification, containment, procedure, exposure route, workforce, waste handling and emergency readiness.
HSE biosafety guidance is agent-, facility-, activity-, worker-, control- and time-specific and is not an exact parcel-level public-health probability.
PPE performance depends on selection, compatibility, fit, condition, maintenance, wearer behaviour, task and exposure environment.
HSE PPE guidance is equipment-, wearer-, task-, hazard-, maintenance- and time-specific and is not an exact parcel-level protection probability.
Health-surveillance value depends on the hazard, exposure, test validity, frequency, worker participation, clinical competence and follow-up action.
HSE surveillance evidence is worker-, hazard-, exposure-, test-, control- and time-specific and is not an exact parcel-level illness probability.
Emergency response depends on event type, occupancy, layout, communications, staffing, vulnerable people, equipment and external-service access.
HSE emergency guidance is site-, incident-, workforce-, communication-, equipment- and time-specific and is not an exact parcel-level casualty probability.
Construction-fire risk depends on project phase, materials, temporary works, ignition sources, occupancy, compartmentation, access and emergency controls.
HSE construction-fire guidance is project-, phase-, material-, occupancy-, control- and time-specific and is not an exact parcel-level fire probability.
Excavation risk depends on soil, depth, support, water, nearby structures, buried services, plant, weather and inspection quality.
HSE excavation guidance is ground-, structure-, service-, plant-, worker-, control- and time-specific and is not an exact parcel-level collapse probability.
Demolition risk depends on structure, sequence, method, temporary stability, adjacent property, exclusion zones, plant and competent supervision.
HSE demolition guidance is structure-, method-, contractor-, site-, public-interface- and time-specific and is not an exact parcel-level collapse probability.
Chainsaw risk depends on task, tree, terrain, saw condition, competence, PPE, weather, public access and emergency rescue arrangements.
HSE chainsaw guidance is operator-, equipment-, tree-, terrain-, control- and time-specific and is not an exact parcel-level injury probability.
Livestock risk depends on species, temperament, facilities, task, worker competence, public access, dogs, weather and animal condition.
HSE livestock guidance is animal-, facility-, handler-, visitor-, task-, control- and time-specific and is not an exact parcel-level injury probability.
TB risk depends on infectiousness, duration and closeness of contact, ventilation, immunity, living conditions, diagnosis and treatment timing.
UKHSA TB guidance is person-, contact-, setting-, host-, diagnostic-, treatment- and time-specific and is not an exact parcel-level infection probability.
Avian-influenza risk depends on virus genotype, infected species, exposure intensity, PPE, symptoms, host factors, testing and antiviral timing.
UKHSA A(H5) evidence is incident-, animal-, person-, exposure-, intervention- and time-specific and is not an exact parcel-level infection probability.
Food-allergy risk depends on the allergen, dose, cross-contact, recipe, labelling, staff communication, consumer susceptibility and emergency response.
FSA allergen evidence is food-, ingredient-, process-, business-, consumer- and time-specific and is not an exact parcel-level allergic-reaction probability.
Medical-device risk depends on device model, indication, software, maintenance, user, patient, environment, corrective action and communication timing.
MHRA safety evidence is product-, incident-, user-, patient-, corrective-action- and time-specific and is not an exact parcel-level harm probability.
RIDDOR applicability depends on employment status, work relationship, diagnosis, injury type, duration, causation and the specific regulatory category.
HSE RIDDOR guidance is incident-, worker-, diagnosis-, causation-, reporting-rule- and time-specific and is not an exact parcel-level accident probability.
